# NOTES: THE TOP OF THE WORLD (Ethel M. Dell, 1920; Gutenberg #12360)

Single book, no separate volumes. Parts I–IV, with chapters numbered per part.

## Dedication/Epigraph
- Dedicated "to the precious memory of my mother"; epigraph: "The years shall not outgo my thinking of thee."
- Prefatory poem (3 stanzas): "top of the world" reached "by faith and love / And God's goodness to my soul"; "one I love / Who has promised to wait for me." Refrain-like closing line: "God's goodness over all."

## PART I
**Ch I – Advice.** Vinery at Ingleton Manor. Old head gardener **Jeffcott** (hoary beard) tells **Sylvia Ingleton** (tawny hair, red-brown eyes wide apart, pride of race) she should marry. She says only one man she could marry, "not ready for me yet"; loyal to **Guy Ranger**, engaged ~5 years (since she was 18; he was 25ish, seven years older). Jeffcott warns: "he's been living every minute of it." Guy, son of squire's bailiff (Ranger yeoman family, public-school educated), was banished by squire **Gilbert Ingleton** to South Africa to join a cousin farming; may return and ask Sylvia if he succeeds. Sylvia's mother (**Mrs. Ingleton**, née unnamed) died 3 years earlier; Sylvia was actual mistress of the Manor. Sylvia turns 25 in 2 years, when she inherits money from mother, to become independent. Squire's new bride **Mrs. Emmott** (widow, vulgar, iron will, jealous) married him within 2 months of meeting in the North; wedding ~6 weeks before. Return from Italian lakes honeymoon in September; Sylvia prepared west bedroom. Guy's letter lies on hall table; Sylvia hides it in her dress as car arrives.

**Ch II – The New Mistress.** Mrs. Ingleton (Caroline), tall, handsome, assertive, embraces Sylvia; wants "cosiness," calls Manor "archaic," "convent." Insists on "Mother"; Sylvia refuses, offers "Madam" in place. Mrs. Ingleton: "You shall call me Madam!" Neighbour **George Preston**, M.F.H., rich (Turf money), clean-shaven, horsey legs, loud, calls Sylvia "Cherry-ripe," pinches her fingers; wants to marry her. Mrs. Ingleton agrees to help Preston for "diamonds." Bliss is the butler. Vicar/neighbour **Vernon Eversley** and **Mr. Preston over the way** mentioned.

**Ch III – The Whip-Hand.** Breakfast: Mrs. Ingleton vows to marry Sylvia to Preston within a year; squire agrees to leave matter to her ("the other fellow" = Guy). Squire has given up hunting at her request. Sylvia rides horse **Winnie**; groom **George** (the groom, not Preston). Mrs. Ingleton: "whip-hand is mine"; locks/threats; Sylvia leaves room. Mrs. Ingleton calls her "little viper." Breakfast at 8:30 rule.

**Ch IV – The Victor.** Hunt Ball at Town Hall. Sylvia met Guy at her debut ball 5 years ago. Preston proposed at last year's ball. Guy's letters have stopped for weeks. Vernon Eversley says he saw an engagement announcement in paper ("He's a dashed lucky man"). Preston has scrawled his name on her dance card. In a secluded corner Preston pressures her; she says she'll cable Guy first; agrees "if you like" to marry Preston if Guy doesn't answer; they are "provisionally" engaged; no kissing. She feels defeated.

**Ch V – The Miracle.** Next morning Sylvia confronts Mrs. Ingleton about suppressed letters; learns (from postman **Evans** via Jeffcott) Guy's letter came on Friday; last Guy letter she received was 6+ weeks ago, the day squire brought Madam home. Sylvia storms at Mrs. Ingleton ("You took them!"), declares she will never sleep under same roof again. Announces she is going to Guy. Preston laughs; squire says "She's my daughter—not yours." Squire unlocks boudoir door; tells Caroline to leave her alone; says he won't stop her. Preston leaves, declining Mrs. Ingleton's support. Mrs. Ingleton retires to bed.

## PART I (continued)
**Ch VI – The Land of Strangers.** Journey to Ritzen (Cape Colony railway, veldt); Guy had cabled he'd meet her at Ritzen. Ritzen is nearest station to Blue Hill Farm (20 miles away). Guy's welcome cold; he has beard, is changed, calculating. Sylvia sees man who is not Guy: **Burke Ranger**, Guy's cousin ("I am Burke Ranger—his cousin"). Burke says Guy is "changed," tells her to go home and marry someone else; she refuses. Burke says Guy is not ill (later a lie). Burke gives her a room at a Ritzen hotel.

**Ch VII – The Wrong Turning.** Next morning Burke at breakfast; she realizes she mistook him for Guy. Burke reveals Guy "took the wrong turning," drinks; sent cable "blind drunk"; has delirium tremens ("That was a lie"). Sylvia insists on seeing Guy; Burke takes her by cart; she promises not to marry Guy "as a way out" ("I promise you I won't do anything damn' foolish for the sake of—sentiment").

**Ch VIII – The Comrade.** Cart ride 20 miles; they cross **Ritter Spruit** (dry watercourse, becomes flood). Picnic at boulder; Burke: "I shall call you The Enchantress"; horse Burke calls... she kisses horse's forehead. Sylvia: wants a "jolly comrade," not a lover. Burke "I shan't let you down." Burke keeps watch over her sleeping.

**Ch IX – The Arrival.** Storm (lightning, rain). Sylvia hurt knee (sprawl on steps). Burke carries her into his bare house; Kaffir woman **Mary Ann** (hideous, lame, obedient). Ritter Spruit flooded; "forty miles" to bridge. Burke says Guy is gone ("Wait till the morning comes!"). Sylvia to sleep in guestroom.

**Ch X – The Dream.** Night; Sylvia plans to live alone; dreams of two horsemen on ravine ledge: Burke (galloping hard, face "of a devil") and Guy; collision; one falls; she can't tell which died. Morning: Burke says Guy "cleared out yesterday morning" (no one knows where). Burke gives her strong hint of "way out."

**Ch XI – The Cross-roads.** Dusk; Sylvia finds Guy's photograph in trunk, weeps. Piet Vreiboom (Boer neighbour; low brow, close-set eyes; mistakenly sees Sylvia with Burke at Ritzen). Burke tells Piet she is his wife (lie). Burke proposes marriage ("I am asking you to marry me"); sets terms: comrades; he won't interfere with liberty; "I can be several kinds of beast, but not the kind you are afraid of." Sylvia accepts; she perceives crossroads.

**Ch XII – The Stale.** (Chapter title in text: "THE STALE" — likely "THE STAKE" in TOC.) Civil marriage at Brennerstadt (mining town further down line). Sylvia wants to avoid English acquaintances. Race to "blasted tree" (skeleton tree with twisted arms); Burke wins; kisses? Sylvia: "Kiss you... if you forbid it"; Sylvia: "we are pals"; she says he can kiss her "if you really want to... only don't be silly." Burke carves words on tree (later revealed as "Fide et Amore"). Burke's irony.

## PART II
**Ch I – Comrades.** Sylvia now works farm, Burke's "overseer"/"junior partner." Burke flogs houseboy **Joe** with sjambok; Sylvia mends Burke's shirt; "Fair Rosamond" (Rose), Kaffir girl. Ride to the **kopje** (sugar-loaf hill; Sylvia wants climb for sunrise; castle "at top of the world" dream). Hut on sand near spruit—Guy's cabin, built by Guy the second year out; Burke had him leave ("I should have skinned him"). Sylvia weeps; Burke's hand on her knee.

**Ch II – The Visitors.** Mr. **Bill Merston** (red-faced, hearty, neighbour 12 miles off) and wife **Matilda Merston** (pale brick complexion, thin, grievances; six children all died in infancy). Matilda: "I hope you like this horrible country"; warns Sylvia; says Burke's young cousin Guy was "sjamboked" and driven out. Sylvia defends Burke.

**Ch III – The Bargain.** Evening at kopje; Burke's "I feel as if I have caught a very rare, shy bird." Sylvia asks Burke to find Guy and save him; Burke agrees "on one condition": a "straight game." Burke reveals (via Merston) Guy tends bar at Hoffstein's miners' saloon in Brennerstadt.

**Ch IV – The Capture.** Brennerstadt; Burke meets Irish friend **Donovan (Donovan) Kelly**, manager of diamond mine; Kelly mentions raffle of **Wilbraham's diamond** (flawed, worth thousands; tickets; draw end of week). Burke and Kelly go to Hoffstein's in sandstorm; Kelly lures Guy out; Burke seizes Guy; Guy drunk, "Let me go!"

**Ch V – The Good Cause.** Burke confines Guy in hotel room. Guy attacks; Burke's chin cut by glass; Guy on floor; Burke forces him; Guy breaks down; Burke's reflection on Guy's weakness and Sylvia.

**Ch VI – The Return.** Sylvia prepares a hut for Guy. Sylvia on kopje/road waiting for Guy; Burke returns alone ("He has gone back to his own cabin"); Burke kisses her "You witch!"; she says "I'm nearly squeezed to death"; she kisses him "Partner dear"; confused comradeship.

**Ch VII – The Guest.** Guy arrives at farm (Sylvia first sees him; thin, ravaged, "Oh, Guy! How ill you look!"). Guy: "Bless your heart!" Sylvia ruined. Guy coughs; Burke tells Sylvia to let Guy go. Guy says "Two's company and three's the deuce." Sylvia: "I'll save him." Burke: "Don't perish in the attempt!" "You are" [indispensable].

**Ch VIII – The Interruption.** Sylvia and Burke in sitting room; Burke: "Sylvia, I'm going to tell you something" — interrupted by shot: Guy attempts suicide (revolver shot) at Blue Hill; Guy's body across threshold; Burke locks revolver in cupboard; says "It couldn't [be accident]." Burke rides off to fetch doctor.

**Ch IX – The Abyss.** Sylvia watches Guy; "Will you forgive me... for making a boss shot!" Guy: "It's hell for me—either way." Sylvia kisses his forehead: "God bless you!"

**Ch X – The Desire to Live.** Dr **Saul Kieff** (Jewish-looking, sleek black hair, onyx eyes, clawlike hands, "raven") arrives with Burke. Kieff: Guy must "desire to live"; "Women were made for sacrifice." Burke kisses sleeping Sylvia ("Good night, dear—Guy!").

**Ch XI – The Remedy.** Kieff uses morphine (remedy from leather case). Guy: "Hullo—darling!" Guy holds Sylvia's hand: "Kiss me, little sweetheart!" Burke dismisses Kieff; says he has "helped him on his way." Burke: "if you ever touch that stuff again, my faith in you will be gone." Burke's claim: "I shall claim [my right] some day."

## PART III
**Ch I – The New Era.** Kieff gives Sylvia morphine for insomnia; she surrenders; Burke discovers marks; Burke sends Kieff away ("He is on his way back to Ritzen or Brennerstadt"). Sylvia apologises: "Please don't be angry."

**Ch II – (Chapter XI in text titled "Into Battle").** Guy recovers; Sylvia and Burke clash; Burke: "Make me!" "I'll defy you to do that!" Sylvia gives in: "I give you best, partner."

**Ch III – The Seed.** Visit to Merstons; Matilda: "Are you still enjoying the Garden of Eden?" Matilda's sympathy; "seed of friendship."

**Ch IV – Mirage.** Sylvia's depression; cuts Fair Rosamond with riding switch; Guy comforts her; Guy: "Why did you marry him?" Sylvia: "I married him because he was so like you."

**Ch V – Everybody's Friend.** Sand-storm; Burke kisses Sylvia in anger; she finds key to strong-box dropped; Donovan Kelly arrives (introduces himself, "late of His Majesty's Imperial Yeomanry"; horse "St. Peter").

**Ch VI – The Hero.** Burke, Guy, Kelly; Burke saved by Guy from burning shed at Vreiboom's; Kieff at Vreiboom's; Guy drinks; Sylvia stops him ("Please, Guy").

**Ch VII – The Net.** Guy and Sylvia at night; "Love that hath us in the net"; Guy: "you are mine"; Sylvia: "I love you... only as a friend."

**Ch VIII – The Summons.** Burke leaves to help Merston (fell from horse); Sylvia accuses Burke; Burke: "Let's go to the top of the world by ourselves!"

**Ch IX – For the Sake of the Old Love.** Sylvia finds strong-box key in lock; cigarette in envelope; money gone; Guy took it; she resolves to find Guy alone.

**Ch X – The Bearer of Evil Tidings.** Kieff at farm tells Kelly that Sylvia has gone to Brennerstadt with Guy (lie); Kelly distressed.

**Ch XI – The Sharp Corner.** Sylvia travels to Brennerstadt by train (breakdown); arrives at hotel; sleeps; Burke appears: "Why are you here?" Accuses her of posing as Guy's wife; she says "That was a mistake" and cites her defence.

**Ch XII – The Cost.** Sylvia confesses devotion; Burke: "So... you have made your choice—and counted the cost?" "You will know—some day." Sylvia's sacrifice.

## PART IV
**Ch I – Sand of the Desert.** Kelly, morning; Burke finds Guy at Hoffstein's (Kieff's opium); Kelly says money was Guy's gamble (diamond tickets). Burke: "Let him go!" Sylvia's speech: "Will you ever forgive me?" Silence begins.

**Ch II – The Skeleton Tree.** Kelly and Sylvia ride; Sylvia tells Kelly: Burke's key, Guy took money; reveals Kieff's lies at Vreiboom's. Kelly: "Burke loves him like a brother." Sylvia sees words on tree: **"Fide et Amore"** (By Faith and Love); "I found out how to get to the top of the world."

**Ch III – The Punishment.** Kieff in hotel mocks Sylvia; Burke thrashes Kieff publicly; Kieff apologizes; Kieff collapses.

**Ch IV – The Evil Thing.** Burke: "You will never have anything more to do with him"; Sylvia finds money in envelope from Kelly ("Yours, D. K."). Kieff found dead (opium overdose) at Hoffstein's. Burke's dark silence.

**Ch V – The Land of Blasted Hopes.** Kelly declares Kieff's death. Sylvia and Burke return to Blue Hill; she intends to restore money; Guy kneels by her bed in moonlight; "Oh, Guy—my own Guy—come to me!"; Guy leaves.

**Ch VI – The Parting.** Sylvia returns money to strong-box (Burke caught her). Burke gives her to Merstons' farm; "Good-bye!" Kiss from the wheel.

**Ch VII – Piet Vreiboom.** Sylvia works with Matilda; Burke's letter ("I want you... I am coming to-morrow to fetch you back"). Piet Vreiboom visits; Sylvia confides to Matilda that she was engaged to Guy.

**Ch VIII – Out of the Depths.** Storm; Guy at window claims he won the Wilbraham diamond; "borrowed" money from strong-box; Sylvia refuses him; he attempts violence; medication; Guy confesses; "Fetch Burke."

**Ch IX – The Meeting.** Burke rides to Merstons' at dawn; sees Sylvia; confronts Guy in guest-hut ("I'll meet you in my own time"); Guy: "Your wife... is incorruptible."

**Ch X – The Truth.** Burke and Matilda talk; Matilda tells Burke Sylvia loved Guy; Burke: "I am going back."

**Ch XI – The Storm.** Drought; Burke at farm; devastating storm; Burke rides Diamond (Sylvia's horse) to hut on sand.

**Ch XII – The Sacrifice.** Flood; Burke reaches hut; Sylvia is there with Guy (ill); Burke's temptation; he saves Guy; Sylvia rides Diamond with Guy; Burke and Sylvia rescued; hut swept away.

**Ch XIII – By Faith and Love.** Guy dies; Burke and Sylvia reconcile; Guy's last words "never loved anyone but you"; Burke says he loved Guy too; Sylvia confesses love; Guy's gift—Wilbraham's diamond; Sylvia and Burke plan to visit England, then return; final words: "By faith—and love, my darling."

## KEY CHARACTERS
- **Sylvia Ingleton** (later Ranger): heroine, 23–24, red-brown eyes, tawny hair.
- **Guy Ranger**: lover, weak, alcoholic/morphine-addicted; dies in flood.
- **Burke Ranger**: Guy's cousin, Sylvia's husband; strong, grey eyes.
- **Gilbert Ingleton** (squire, father); **Caroline Ingleton/Mrs. Emmott** (stepmother).
- **George Preston** (M.F.H.; "Captain Preston"); **Jeffcott**; **Bliss** (butler); **Mrs. Hadlow**.
- **Mary Ann** (Kaffir woman); **Joe** (house boy); **Fair Rosamond** (Rose); **Hans Schafen** (Dutch overseer).
- **Bill & Matilda Merston**.
- **Piet Vreiboom** (Boer neighbour).
- **Saul Kieff** (doctor/villain, dies by opium).
- **Donovan Kelly** (Irish friend; horse "St. Peter").
- **Hoffstein** (bar owner; Hoffstein's tavern); **Wilbraham** (diamond owner).
- Places: the Manor; Ritzen (railway station); Brennerstadt (mining town); Blue Hill Farm; Ritter Spruit; the kopje; the skeleton tree; Merstons' farm; hut on sand.
- Horses: Winnie (Sylvia's early mount), Diamond (Sylvia's wedding gift, black with white head mark).
